newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair sees possible 1996 net loss.
newsitem.headline: Swissair sees possible 1996 net loss.

text.p: Swissair AG said it expected to report a group profit before extraordinary items for 1996, but cautioned that any adjustment in the value of its stake in Sabena could result in a net loss for the year.
Philippe Bruggisser, Swissair's chief operating officer, said in remarks prepared for a news conference that operating results were slightly better than last year until the end of September.
However, with Swissair's airline division "suffering a deeply disappointing October", Bruggisser said the annual operating result might be below the 1995 results.
Bruggisser said the expectation for an ordinary profit did not include the impact of Sabena.
Swissair's first half loss was widened by around 36 million by Sabena's loss and he expects the Belgian carrier to post a loss for the second half also.

"The extent of any value adjustment to our holding in Sabena has not yet been decided; any such decision is unlikely to be taken until Sabena's annual result is known. Needless to say, any value adjustment of this kind would lead to a corresponding reduction in group profit for the year, and could concievable push that result into the red," Bruggisser said.
